2026-06-29.title: Type-Safe APIs: From Zod to End-to-End Inference

trending.heading: Trending for you
trending.content:
## Validation is having a moment

Teams are standardizing on **runtime schema validation** at the network boundary. The headline: validate once, infer everywhere.

- **Parse, don't validate.** A parsed object carries proof of its shape in the type system.
- **Single source of truth.** One schema generates both the runtime check and the static type.
- **Better errors.** Structured validation errors beat `undefined is not a function` at 2am.

continueToLearn.heading: Continue to learn
continueToLearn.content:
## Inferring types from schemas

Yesterday you saw why validation matters. Today: how a schema becomes a type for free.

```ts
const User = z.object({ id: z.string(), age: z.number() });
type User = z.infer<typeof User>; // { id: string; age: number }
```

> One declaration, two guarantees: runtime safety and compile-time types.

## Components that respond to their container, not the viewport

**Container queries** let a card adapt based on the space it's given — finally making truly reusable components possible.

- Style by available width, not screen width.
- Drop the media-query gymnastics for component layouts.
- Ship one component that looks right in a sidebar and a full-width hero.

2026-06-25.title: Postgres for App Developers: Indexes You Actually Need

trending.heading: Trending for you
trending.content:
## The four indexes that cover 90% of app queries

- **B-tree** for equality and ranges (the default, usually right).
- **Partial** for `WHERE status = 'active'` style hot paths.
- **Composite** when you always filter by the same two columns together.
- **GIN** for JSONB and full-text search.

> Indexes speed reads and slow writes — add them where you read often, not everywhere.

continueToLearn.heading: Continue to learn
continueToLearn.content:
## Reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE

```sql
EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM digests WHERE user_id = $1;
```

Look for `Seq Scan` on large tables — that's your signal a missing index is hurting.

## Accessibility is a build-time concern now

- Prefer **semantic HTML** before reaching for ARIA.
- Every interactive element needs a **focus state** and a **name**.
- Test with a keyboard only — if you can't Tab to it, neither can many users.

## The first rule of ARIA

> The first rule of ARIA is: don't use ARIA if a native element does the job. A `<button>` beats a `<div role="button">` every time.
